decision_rationale: Stem asks 'what does this grant best illustrate' — the student selects which concept the charter exemplifies; the explanation is already given in the options, so the cognitive task is identification of a historical concept/development (1.A), not explaining it (1.B). Recheck wins.

The item asks what explains the post-1800 population surge; the key treats it as a demographic consequence of mass European migration — an effect of migration (6.7), not the causes of migration (6.6). Recheck wins.

The Mandate was created by the post-WWI peace settlement that divided Ottoman lands — the postwar order that set the stage for later decolonization (8.1), not the decolonization movements themselves (8.5). Recheck wins.

The source is narrative, not an argument; the student uses its details (enrollment among attendants of honor above courtiers) as evidence supporting the broader claim about Mongol recruitment practice — the evidence-to-argument move of 3.D, not identifying a claim stated in the source (3.A). First wins.

Battuta's descriptive details serve as evidence supporting the claim that Mongols favored foreign Muslims as administrators — 3.D's 'claims or evidence support an argument' move, not a claim stated in the source (3.A). First wins.

The China source's claims (dense population, existing bureaucracy) are used as evidence supporting the broader claim about Mongol adaptation (direct rule vs tribute-taking) — 3.D evidence-to-argument reasoning, not identifying a claim in the source. First wins.

Bernier's reverse-tribute detail is evidence supporting the claim of negotiated Mughal sovereignty — the student explains how the source's claims support an argument (3.D), rather than identifying a claim stated in the source (3.A). First wins.

Skill: 'best illustrates which relationship' asks the student to identify the broader economic context the triangular trade sits in (slave-produced commodities fueling European growth) — 4.A identification of context, not 4.B explanation of situatedness. Topic: the triangular trade and plantation slavery are the systems sustaining maritime empires (4.5 Maintained and Developed), not social hierarchies (4.7). Recheck wins both.

Rodney's 1974 argument targets European extraction via the slave trade and colonialism as the cause of underdevelopment — it concerns how maritime empires were maintained through wealth extraction (4.5), not changing social hierarchies (4.7). Recheck wins.

Stem asks 'best explains why' Europeans used spheres of influence in China — the student explains how that development is situated in the broader context (China too large/organized to conquer, unlike directly colonized regions) — 4.B, not 4.A identification. Recheck wins.

The item does not compare Ferry's argument against the map's argument — the map has no argument, only an outcome. Both sources' claims function as evidence supporting the single conclusion that moral rhetoric masked economic/strategic motives — 3.D, not 3.C (which requires comparing two sources' arguments/main ideas). First wins.

The GDP table is a non-text source with no stated claim; the student uses its 1944-46 collapse as evidence supporting the argument that bombing and defeat devastated the economy — 3.D's evidence-supports-argument move, not identifying a claim in the source (3.A). First wins.

'Best illustrates which of the following about the United States in 1938' asks the student to identify the source's historical situation (contempt for fascism amid official neutrality) — 2.A identification, not 2.B explanation. Recheck wins.

Skill: the program's paired claims (independence + confiscation) are evidence supporting the argument that nationalism and socialism were inseparable for Ho — 3.D evidence-to-argument reasoning. Topic: Ho's 1930 program is fundamentally an anti-colonial program; the core development is decolonization (8.5), with communist content paired into it, not the spread of communism per se (8.4). Recheck wins topic; first wins skill.
'Primarily enabled the Inca state to' asks the student to identify the function of the road system as a development — identification (1.A), not explanation of the process (1.B). Recheck wins.

The celadon vase illustrates Korea's luxury production and participation in East Asian exchange networks — the cultural consequences of connectivity (2.5), not the Silk Roads network itself (2.1). Recheck wins.

The Grand Embassy portrait reflects Peter's Westernization program — the administrative transformation of the Russian Empire (3.2 Empires: Administration), not territorial expansion (3.1). First wins.

'Best understood as' asks the student to identify what Osaka Castle represents (a display of centralized power over a unified Japan) — identification of the concept (1.A), not explanation of the development (1.B). First wins.

'Organized primarily around' asks the student to identify which broader development the Tordesillas-meridian map illustrates (Spain/Portugal's exclusive exploration zones) — identification of the context (4.A), not 4.B explanation. Recheck wins.

'Organized primarily around' asks the student to identify the settlement's organizing feature from the Castello Plan (harbor/warehouses for commerce) — identification (1.A), not explanation of the difference (1.B). First wins.

The 1776 Hudson Bay map charts rivers and coasts for the fur-trade logistics of an existing maritime empire — the maintaining/developing of the empire (4.5), not its initial establishment (4.4). Recheck wins.

'What does the wording reveal about the author's purpose' asks the student to identify the connection between de Gouges's preamble and the Revolution's own logic — identification of the connection (5.A), not explanation of how one relates to the other (5.B). First wins. (The rechecker's suggestion of a Sourcing/Situation skill is out of bounds: the hard constraint requires the skill family to match Making Connections.)

Skill: 'what does this image reveal about the character of Russian emancipation' requires explaining the development (top-down reform to preserve autocracy, limited by redemption payments) — 1.B, consistent with prior adjudication convention. Topic: the 1861 emancipation was a state-led modernization measure — 5.6 Government's Role, not a nationalist revolution (5.2). Recheck wins both.

The item asks the student to identify what the British engraving's framing emphasizes — the triumphal depiction of conquest as state expansion (6.2); Cetshwayo's capture is not an indigenous response to expansion (6.3). First wins.

Within the constrained skill family, the student identifies the claim the aerial photograph (a non-text source) supports — 3.A. First wins. (Flag for the content team: the rechecker is right that this item genuinely asks for an explanation of a military-technical development and would fit 1.B better, but the hard constraint requires the skill family to stay in Claims and Evidence.)
